chunks: Al-Abtah was named Abtah because Adam عليه السلام was commanded to lie prostrate in the flat expanse of Jamʿ, so he lay there until dawn broke. Adam عليه السلام was only commanded to make confession so that it would become a sunnah (prophetic tradition) among his descendants.
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله permitted al-ʿAbbās to stay overnight in Makkah during the nights of Minā for the sake of providing water to the pilgrims.

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله only entered ihram from al-Shajarah because when he was taken by night to the heaven, he was at the place aligned with the tree, and it was called out: 'O Muhammad.' He said: 'Labbayk.'
He said: 'Did I not find you an orphan and give shelter, and find you astray and guide?'
So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said: 'Praise, blessing, and sovereignty belong to You; there is no partner for You.' Therefore he entered ihram from al-Shajarah instead of all other places.

As for garlanding the sacrificial camels, it is so that it may be known that it is a sacrificial animal, and its owner may recognize it by the sandal with which he garlands it. Ishʿār was only commanded so that its back would become forbidden to its owner from the point where he marked it, and so that Shaytan would not be able to mount it.

key_terms.الشَّجَرَةِ: al-Shajarah, the miqat from which the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله entered ihram
key_terms.الشَّيْطَانُ: Shaytan, who is mentioned as being unable to mount the marked animal
key_terms.الِاعْتِرَافِ: confession or acknowledgment commanded to Adam عليه السلام as a sunnah for his descendants
key_terms.الْأَبْطَحُ: Al-Abtah, a place whose naming is explained in the narration
key_terms.الْإِشْعَارُ: marking the sacrificial animal to designate it and set restrictions upon its use
key_terms.بَطْحَاءِ جَمْعٍ: the flat expanse of Jamʿ where Adam عليه السلام was commanded to lie prostrate
key_terms.تَقْلِيدُ الْبُدْنِ: garlanding sacrificial camels as a sign of consecration

ai.seo_question: What reasons are given in this hadith for naming al-Abtah, entering ihram from al-Shajarah, and marking sacrificial animals during hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith gathers several reasons connected to hajj rites, sacred places, and prophetic practice. It links certain rituals to earlier sacred history, to the Miʿraj of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, and to practical signs by which sacrificial animals are identified and set apart.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2134 - Al-Abtah was named 'Abtah' because Adam (as) was commanded to prostrate himself in the flat expanse of Jam’ until dawn broke. Adam was commanded to make this confession so that it would become a tradition among his descendants.
The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace and blessings be upon him and his family, granted permission to Al-Abbas to stay in Makkah during the nights of Mina to provide water for the pilgrims.

The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace and blessings be upon him and his family, entered Ihram from the tree (Dhul-Hulayfah) because, when he was taken on the Night Journey to the heavens, he was at the place opposite the tree and was called out, 'O Muhammad.'
He (sw) replied: 'Here I am.'
Then it was said, 'Did We not find you an orphan and shelter you? And We found you wandering and guided you?' (Surah Ad-Duha 93:6-7).

The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, responded: 'All praise, blessings, and sovereignty belong to You; You have no partner.'
For this reason, He (sw) entered Ihram from the tree instead of any other location.

As for marking the sacrificial animals with necklaces (taqlid), it is so they can be recognized as sacrificial animals, and the owner can identify them by the sandal tied as their necklace. Marking (ish’ar) was commanded to ensure the animal's back would be forbidden for its owner to use once it was marked, and so Satan would not be able to mount it.
